commentary_title: Freight rates gain on Med and UKC routes
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index declined by close to 3 points in week 10 to finish at 106.4. It was a mixed week for the segment as trade activity rose and waned in various regions however, rates on TD20 gained $3 by the end of the week. | The global ballast speed rose last week by around 0.5kn inching closer to 9kn mostly due to increased speed towards the East. Some activity could likely increase Eastward, especially China as indicated by the strong growth in %laden towards the East. Though, as a result, we could see an increase in tonnage ballasting back towards the Suez as well.

commentary_title: Trans-Pacific trade leads the Suezmax demand in week 14
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index softened in week 14, ending the week at 104.2 points. It was a quieter week, especially towards the East with sentiments for week 15 not being very bright. | Tonnage was well supplied in the AG and WAF regions softening rates especially on Eastbound routes. Market in the USG and Brazil were most active last week both showing an uptick in their trade activity. | The ballast speed in the West increased by 1 kn over the week as the firm market activity is expected to continue into the next week, causing more ships to ballast Westward. However, Eastbound activity is expected to remain soft in week 15 which will also cause freight rates to weaken.

commentary_title: Tonne-miles index climbs up for the third consecutive week
commentary_summary: The tonne-miles index continued to rise in week 18, from its uptick in week 16 to reach 120.7 points. Robust demand for tonnage on long haul routes helped in pushing up the tonne-mile demand last week as well as freight rates on routes in the West. | With the demand for crude remaining firm, the performance of Suezmax vessels also improved greatly this week with an increase in utilisation despite a decline in repairs and Labour Day holidays subduing market activity in several regions. | Next week is likely to see a positive continuation of the demand for Suezmax vessels especially on the longer haul routes.

commentary_title: Market activity in the Med heats up tonnage demand
commentary_summary: It was an active week in the Suezmax market as freight rates heated up on most routes especially towards the Mediterranean. However, an activity waned towards the end of the week with more owners seeking for contracts amid the heated tonnage demand. | Despite the week starting high, the tonne-miles index fell to 102.8 points as there was more accumulation of tonnage around the ports. | Next week is likely to see some cooling off in the market as charterers will likely seek softer rates before June. Markets are likely to remain firm in the Med while the underway vessels head upwards.

commentary_title: Subdued Suezmax demand to remain the trend
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tanker market has been facing an underwhelming demand this year, which will likely remain weak as we enter the mid-year seasonal lull. The tonne-miles index did see a rise in week 25, ending at 111.9 points as route diversions continued to stretch the Suzmax voyages. | The crude oil demand in Asia has been weak this year, but the %laden in the East saw a slight uptick last week. There was an increase in tonnage underway in the East, which could also include tankers that have newly entered the CPP market. | The markets in the West have also witnessed similar lulls and will likely remain subdued next week, affecting freight rates negatively.

commentary_title: A forward looking week for Suezmaxes ahead
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-mile index saw minimal change in week 29, ending the week at 108.8 points. While markets were generally quieter, demand saw an uptick towards the end of the week. However, the lull throughout the majority of the week caused freight rates to lower, which might prompt cargo owners to continue exerting pressure to keep freight rates down even in the next week. | The markets in the WAF region are likely to remain the most active next week, which could continue to cause rates to weaken. Meanwhile, the laden speed in the East and West showed an increase, pointing towards a more hopeful week for Suezmax tankers.

commentary_title: Suzmax employment remains subdued due to weak seasonal factors
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index declined in week 32, ending the week at 93.4 points. The decline has been continuing since week 27, caused by an overall weakness in oil demand. This has also been reflected in the fleet's utilization, which has been declining since week 25. | There is also strong competition for cargo from the VLCCs. There has also been minimal movement in the markets in the Arabian Gulf region heading Eastward. | The Suezmax market in West Africa remained steady but sentiments for next week are not very optimistic. Freight rates declined on most routes except on routes via the Suez Canal. The Suezmax market is likely to remain subdued in week 33 as well.

commentary_title: Freight rates likely to remain firm next week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax markets saw a firming up of freight rates despite a soft week. The tonne-miles index showed a slight increase of 0.7 points ending the week at 108.2. Freight rates firmed up on most routes and sentiments are high as winter demand is expected to boost tonnage demand in the coming weeks. | China recently released new oil export quotas to boost trade of refined products which is expected to support Suezmax freight rates in the coming weeks. Meanwhile there was some firming of rates in the Med/Black Sea region and the USG to UKC routes which will likely attract more ballast tonnage next week. | Towards West Africa, sentiments remained high but it did not translate to any uptick in trade activity. However, this leaves much potential for Suezmax demand to grow in week 39.

commentary_title: Mixed market sentiments keep freight rates buoyed
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-mile index ended the week at 111.8 points after declining by around 4 points. The week ended with mixed sentiments in the Suezmax market as hurricanes continued to disrupt trade in the West Atlantic regions. | The markets in the UKC also witnessed some softening, with most of the week's gains going towards the MEG, which saw slightly firmer rates. Libyan exports coming back on track also supported the region, attracting more Aframaxes. | While the Westward markets seem likely to be plagued by limitations from weather conditions, markets towards the East remain hopeful for next week.

commentary_title: Winter demand is expected to boost Suezmax activity this week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-mile index ended the week on the softer side at 105.9 points after declining by around 5 points over the week. Utilisation, on the other hand, seems to have headed for a peak for a third time this year. Despite October ending off mild, an uptick in seasonal demand is likely to push up vessel utilisation as well as rates in the coming weeks. | Week 44 started off soft, but more ballast vessels arrived at the USG, which eased rates in the USG-UKC region. It was a slow week overall as vessel speeds declined in both the East and the West. The markets towards the West had shown more enthusiasm as the Chinese demand remained on the weaker side. Week 45 will, however, see more activity with the highest gains on ex-USG routes.

commentary_title: Firmness in the Suezmax market likely to weaken
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index fell in week 47 ending the week at 95.1 points. Despite the index weakening, rates firmed up as market activity improved in the Middle East post the Bahri week. Many vessels headed towards the East, especially to India with some upward push coming from the Med. The tonnage towards the East is likely to increase next week, keeping rates firm. | Activity towards the USG remained buoyant, aided by a steady Aframax market. However, next week might see dullness in the market due to a lack of tonnage demand. | Overall, most of the gains in spot rates came from tonnage demand stemming from the East. This might improve the tonnage underway next week. However, there is likely to be some slowdown in activity in the other regions, keeping more tonnage at the ports, especially the Atlantic and AG.

commentary_title: Suezmax utilisation continue to decline
commentary_summary: The utilisation of Suezmax continued to decline last week due to the ample tonnage list in the Atlantic region, which weighed on the Suezmax rates. Unless demand surges in the pre-Christmas week, the rates are expected to soften for the next two weeks. | Meanwhile, the tonne-mile index remained flat due to a lack of activity. Despite the subdued demand this month, owners are expecting a busier period in January as the country needs to replenish its reserves after the peak demand season.

commentary_title: Suezmax market likely to improve next week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index remained stable in week 2, ending the week at 102.1 points, with market sentiment for Suezmaxes remaining somewhat mixed. On a MoM basis, ports towards the East saw a decline in congestion while ballast speed declined overall last week. | Freight rates remained stable on most routes but could see some firming up next week as tonnage demand in West Africa and Latin America are seemingly starting to pick up. With the VLCC market firming up in the past week, this will likely boost Suezmax demand as the VLCC market tightens.

commentary_title: Eastern Suezmax demand sees a rise ahead of the Lunar New Year
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index improved close to five points ending the week at 89.1 points as the pre-lunar New Year rush caused an uptick in the tonnage demand ahead of the holidays. As a result, week 6 is likely to continue seeing a slight squeeze in the tonnage availability especially for Eastbound cargoes. | A 38% MoM increase in the tonnage at anchor in the West has also been accompanied by a decline in the vessel speeds of both ballast and laden vessels with the tonnage underway declining in tandem. Market activity at the moment remains sluggish but rates continue to be firm. Next week could see some improvement in tonnage demand but will most likely remain on similar levels as in week 5.

commentary_title: Softness in tonnage demand weighs on freight rates
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index continued to improve in week 8, ending the week at 100.3 points. However, this week's rise was slightly flatter than the previous week, with a sharp rise in the number of vessels at ports in the East. Activity was relatively subdued this week due to the lesser availability of cargo, pushing down rates. | Rates declined on most routes except for the Black Sea to Med, which remained intact. Market activity next week is likely to remain on par with week 8, which could result in current rates remaining firm, especially towards the East.

commentary_title: Firm Eastern demand to support freight rates next week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index continued to rise in week 11, ending the week at 116.9 points. It has been continuously rising for the past seven weeks, though utilisation of the Suezmax fleet has seen slight variances. | Freight rates firmed up on most routes especially on ex-MEG routes, as Middle Eastern crude continues to grow in popularity in Eastern markets this year. | Market sentiments for next week are likely to remain positive as firm Suezmax demand in the East seems to have had spillovers in the Western markets as well which will likely continue to push up freight rates overall.

commentary_title: Freight rates decline as tonnage demand weakens
commentary_summary: It was a quieter week in the Suezmax market as freight rates declined on most routes. The tonne-miles index ended the week at 108 points. The markets started off firm towards the East but dwindled as the week went on with tonnage at anchor being more than 20% higher MoM. | Towards the Med, the CPC controversy caused some market disruptions weighing down freight rates. Meanwhile, the market towards West Africa was more positive, attracting more ballast vessels from the Med. Rates are likely to remain sideways next week.

commentary_title: Robust tonnage demand in WAF keeps freight rates high
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index ended the week at 123.4 points, reaching a new high for the year as freight rates have been gaining steadily over the past few weeks. Freight rates increased on several routes towards the West, while they were steadier towards the East. | Market activity towards West Africa was robust throughout the week, which helped push up tonne-mile demand. There was also high tonnage demand in the larger VLCC, which had trickle-down effects on its smaller counterpart. Market sentiments are likely to remain similar next week.

commentary_title: Positive sentiments likely to push up freight rates next week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax market had a slow week with freight rates declining on most routes. Despite this, the utilisation of vessels for this segment has been continuously rising as activity continues to be stable with more vessels being fixed at lower rates. | The market towards the MEG showed some improvement last week with more enquiries expected to push up rates next week. Similarly, a good level of enquiries towards West Africa for transatlantic voyages are expected to push up rates next week due to a decline in the tonnage supply.

commentary_title: Growth in tonnage demand to support rates next week
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index rose for the second week in a row after facing a massive dip the previous weeks. Vessel utilisation seems to have been on a similar trajectory with both the global laden and ballast speeds increasing WoW. | The rates had positive gains on most routes owing to a rise in tonnage demand. Both the long and short-haul routes had spot rates increasing in the previous week. With the summer driving season coming soon, rates are likely to remain supported next week as well.

commentary_title: Ceasefire in the Middle East causes rates to weaken
commentary_summary: It was an overall soft week for the Suezmax market. The easing of tensions in the Middle East due to the ceasefire has caused rates to dwindle, especially for the ex-MEG routes. | The tonne miles index did show an uptick amid all the new developments in the Middle East. While the risk of an oil supply cut due to the possible closure of the Strait of Hormuz briefly spurred oil demand, increasing the underway laden vessels, freight rates will likely weaken next week.

commentary_title: Suezmax rates firm up as loadings increase in the West
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index increased in week 32, ending at 114.7 points, rising by close to 13 points from the previous week. | Suezmax earnings have been firming up on most major routes as vessel loadings jumped in week 32. In particular, trade from West Africa to the UKC saw robust activity last week, and the tonnage supply increasingly tightened as the week went by. | Freight rates will likely remain firm next week with an upward push from the active VLCC market.

commentary_title: Suezmax tonnage demand to remain stable
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index gained 2 points in week 36, ending at 117.4 points. It was a typical week, and freight rates remained stable overall. Much of the market activity is aimed towards end- Sept and early October dates, and minimal activity could be seen in the coming weeks. | The average speed for both ballast and laden vessels increased in the East and West. In comparison, the %laden has weakened WoW. This will likely result in more vessels at anchor and fewer vessels underway next week. | Next week, the WAF-UKC trade will likely remain positive with higher gains on freight rates.

commentary_title: Lackluster week in the Suezmax market
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index declined for the third week, ending at 102.1 points. Meanwhile, there was an uptick in vessels at anchor MoM with a corresponding decline in vessels underway. | it was a quiet week for the Sezmax market as rates declined WoW. Tonnage demand towards the UKC was weak causing rates on WAF to UKC to decline further. | There were some trickle-down effects from the relatively firmer demand in the VLCC markets, supporting rates on ex-USG. | Freight rates are, however, likely to weaken further in week 37 due to waning tonnage demand in the VLCC segment.

commentary_title: A mixed week for the Suezmax markets, trend to continue next week
commentary_summary: It was an overall stable week for the Suezmax market, as activity in most regions continued at the same levels as last week. The tonne- miles index declined slightly, ending the week at 117.9 points. | Market activity was relatively dull towards the East due to weak VLCC demand weighing down on Suezmax freight rates. Next week is likely to continue on the same trend. | Towards the West, increased market activity in the US also helped push up some rates on ex-WAF routes. Freight rates are likely to remain stable next week.

commentary_title: Stable utilisation and strong tonne-miles keep Suezmax earnings supported
commentary_summary: Suezmax utilisation remained stable at 90%, although slightly lower MoM, but above last year (89.7%), while the tonne-mile index grew by 8.4 point, suggesting improving vessel demand. | Despite an 11.6% MoM fall in bunker prices, vessel speeds have not changed significantly, particularly in the East, preventing lower fuel costs from translating into higher fleet supply. | Recent Iran-US developments have likely added short-term volatility to vessel positioning, particularly in the Middle-East. The brief de-escalation followed by a rapid breakdown, may have influenced regional fleet movements, contributing to the observed tightening in the East. However, the impact appears temporary, with no clear disruption to tonne-mile demand.

commentary_title: Firm utilisation persists despite lower tonne-miles and rising eastern availability
commentary_summary: Despite suezmax utilisation remaining firm at 91%, the tonne-mile index fell from 118.3 to 104.8 as a number of long-haul Atlantic to Asia voyages reached their discharge destinations. This increased vessel availability in the east and reduced the share of laden tonnage, indicating that voyage completions outpaced fresh long-haul cargo fixing . | Atlantic loading regions appeared to remain the primary source of demand, with vessels continuing to be absorbed from waiting positions and re-entering active trading. | Despite the increase in Eastern vessel presence, the share of laden vessels in the East fell 5.4 percentage points MoM, suggesting many recently arrived ships had already discharged cargoes and transitioned into ballast status. | Port congestion across key eastern regions remained relatively limited, indicating that operational delays had little impact on effective vessel availability.

commentary_title: Rising congestion offsets weaker tonne-mile demand in the Suezmax segment
commentary_summary: Suezmax utilisation stood at 90%, down by 1.8 percentage points WoW and 1.2 percentage points MoM. The tonne-mile index declined from 103.2 to 100.7 WoW and by 10.6% YoY. The weaker tonne-mile environment suggests softer long-haul trade demand compared with last year. | Supply tightened further as global tonnage at anchor rose by 2.2 mdwt and laden anchor days increased 22.2%, reducing prompt vessel availability. Congestion remained most pronounced in the Atlantic basin and Indian ocean, while regional anchorage trends diverged with anchored capacity falling 8.9% MoM in the west but rising 12% in the east, pointing to ongoing fleet repositioning. | Vessel speeds remained broadly stable despite bunker prices surging 33.4% MoM to $845 per tonne. Ballast speeds declined mostly in both basins, while laden speeds remained largely unchanged. Although the share of laden vessels fell by 5.1 percentage points in the east and 7.3 percentage points in the west, high utilisation, rising anchorage activity and persistent regional congestion continue to offset weaker tonne-mile growth, keeping Suezmax market supportive.

commentary_title: Atlantic strength underpins utilisation amid muted tonne-mile growth.
commentary_summary: Suezmax utilisation remained firm at 91.6% while tonne-mile index declined slightly to 104.2 . The gap between rising utilisation and softer tonne-mile demand indicates that a larger proportion of Suezmax employment is being generated by shorter regional trades rather than long-haul inter-basin crude movements. | Tonnage underway in western regions increased notably, pointing to stronger cargo execution and vessel employment across Atlantic-loading areas including West Africa, the Mediterranean, Brazil and the US. | Indian Ocean laden volumes remained elevated, reflecting continued crude movements through traditional Middle East to Asia trade corridors, although not at levels sufficient to significantly boost tonne-mile demand.

commentary_title: Suezmax market remained balanced as stronger vessel supply offset trading activity.
commentary_summary: Suezmax utilisation remained relatively resilient at 89% during the week, even as the tonne-mile index eased to 106.3 from 109.0. The modest decline in demand was largely offset by ongoing crude trading activity; however, improving vessel availability, easing congestion and faster vessel turnaround times increased effective fleet supply and prevented utilisation from strengthening further. | Vessel availability increased in the East, with anchored capacity rising 12%, pointing to a growing pool of prompt tonnage across Middle East and Asian loading regions. | Congestion dynamics were mixed across regions. Laden tonnage waiting in China declined noticeably, signalling faster discharge operations and quicker vessel recycling back into the market. Meanwhile, congestion involving laden vessels in the Indian Ocean increased during the week, although the tighter regional conditions were not strong enough to offset broader improvements in vessel availability elsewhere.

commentary_title: Suezmax utilisation strengthens as Eastern markets drive vessel employment
commentary_summary: Suezmax utilisation rose to 92.0% in Week 41, up 2.2 percentage points MoM and 2.0 percentage points YoY, reflecting firmer fleet employment despite a softer demand backdrop. The tonne-mile index stood at 110.0, down 6.3% YoY, indicating that while crude trade volumes remain relatively resilient, shorter-haul movements and evolving trade patterns continue to temper underlying transport demand. | East of Suez provided the main source of support, with the share of laden vessels rising by 4.3 percentage points MoM. Increased Indian Ocean anchorage volumes and a 17.9% rise in eastern anchored capacity reflected stronger vessel absorption, while a 45.1% decline in western anchored capacity indicated improving vessel availability in the Atlantic market. | Higher utilisation was partly offset by improving vessel availability. Laden anchor days fell 11.4% on a four-week moving-average basis, while East ballast speeds increased 5.1% MoM, supporting faster vessel turnover and greater effective fleet supply, which limited further freight-rate upside.
